AM10G-01.note: 62 - 2(23) = 16. Pure arithmetic on the isosceles definition; the only geometry is 'two sides congruent'. Distractors 39 (62-23) and 31 (62/2) both satisfy the triangle inequality, so no elimination shortcut. Easy, early-form.

AM10G-02.note: side 10, diagonal 10*sqrt(2) = 14.142. 28.3 = 20*sqrt(2) (uses perimeter as side), 20 = half perimeter. Clean.

AM10G-03.note: CW 90: (x,y) -> (y,-x) = (6,4). CCW image (-6,-4) is present as a distractor, and 'CLOCKWISE' is capitalised, so the direction is not ambiguous. Medium-easy.

AM10G-04.note: P = A + (1/4)(B-A) = (-2+3, 1+2). (4,5) is the midpoint, (7,7) is the 3:1 reversal. Ratio orientation is stated as AP:PB so no second reading. Medium.

AM10G-05.note: (10+2w)(24+2w) - 240 = 240 -> w^2 + 17w - 60 = 0 -> w = 3 (other root -20, rejected). 'OUTSIDE' and 'uniform width' close the usual loopholes. Late-form difficulty.

AM10G-06.note: r = sqrt(25+144) = 13. Distances of the other options: (4,11) 12, (0,12) sqrt(185), (9,-1) 5. Exactly one at 13. Medium.

AM10G-07.note: Cup is point down, so the water is a similar cone of half the height: ratio (1/2)^3 = 1/8. 1/2 is the linear-ratio trap. Requires the cube-of-ratio fact, which is late-form.

AM10G-08.note: d*tan32 = (d-20)*tan47 -> d = 20tan47/(tan47-tan32) = 47.927; h = 29.95 -> 29.9. Two-triangle elevation with a system; genuinely hard, one of the few here. Distractors 21.4 = 20tan47 and 12.5 = 20tan32 are the one-step errors.

AM10G-09.note: Diagonal 26 is the diameter, r = 13, area 169pi. 676pi uses the diagonal as radius, 26pi confuses circumference/area. The inscribed-rectangle fact (diagonal = diameter) is load-bearing. Medium. Shares the numbers 10 and 24 with AM10G-05.

AM10G-10.note: Horizontal base 12 at y=3, height 7, area 42. Shoelace agrees. 84 omits the 1/2. Easy-medium.

AM10G-11.note: Side of a regular hexagon equals the circumradius, so perimeter = 60.0. 62.8 is the circle's circumference, 69.3 = 6*10*sqrt(3)/... the apothem-based error. Minor tell: 'to the nearest tenth of a centimeter' implies a non-terminating value and the key is exactly 60.0, which nudges a careful student AWAY from the key; the rounding instruction is unearned here. Easy-medium.

AM10G-12.note: Slant height 10 with half-edge 6 gives height 8; V = (1/3)(144)(8) = 384. 480 is the trap that uses the slant height as the altitude, so the Pythagorean step is load-bearing. Slant height is explicitly defined in the stem, which removes the usual ambiguity. Medium.

AM10G-13.note: Base 7 (7-24-25), pulled to 15, new height sqrt(625-225) = 20. Ladder length is implicitly constant; the stem says 'still resting against the wall' which carries that. 7 and 15 are the intermediate values. Medium.

AM10N-02.note: 9 - 12i + 4i^2 = 5 - 12i. 13 - 12i is the sign error on i^2. Medium.

AM10N-03.note: 5,15,45,135,405,1215 sums to 1820; formula 5(3^6-1)/2 agrees. Listing six terms is faster than the formula, which keeps this medium rather than hard. 1215 is the 6th term, 3645 the 7th, 364 drops the factor 5.

AM10N-04.note: 51/99 = 17/33. 51/990 is the one-digit-block error, 17/30 = 0.5667. 'in lowest terms' rules out any second reading. Medium.

AM10N-05.note: C(4,2)(2x)^2(-3)^2 = 6*4*9 = 216. Requires binomial theorem or a full careful expansion; late-form. 'Coefficient of x^2' is unambiguous (the sign is positive, and no option is -216 so sign errors are not rewarded).

AM10N-06.note: (AB)_12 = 2*6 + (-1)(-3) = 15. Correct answer; my only complaint is FORMAT: the ACT renders matrices as bracketed arrays, not as prose 'first row 2, -1'. The prose is unambiguous but does not look like a real item. 9 = 12-3 is the sign trap.

AM10N-07.note: 2u = <10,-4>; <10,-4> - <-3,6> = <13,-10>. <7,2> and the rest are the sign/scalar errors. Medium-easy.

AM10N-09.note: Count n coprime to 60: 60*(1/2)(2/3)(4/5) = 16; by sieve, 30 odd, 20 of those not div by 3, 16 of those not div by 5. n=60 correctly excluded. 44 = 60-16. Unusual phrasing for the ACT but within Number & Quantity and solvable by listing; genuinely hard.

AM10S-01.note: Predicted 2.4(12)+15.6 = 44.4; residual 57 - 44.4 = 12.6. The stem defines residual and fixes the sign direction, so -12.6 is properly excluded. Medium.

AM10S-02.note: 9*9*8 = 648 favourable out of 900; 648/900 = 0.72. 0.648 is the trap that divides by 1000 (i.e. forgets the leading digit cannot be 0 restricts the sample space to 900). Hard.
